blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — statin intensity and therapeutic response
stem: A client is prescribed a high-intensity statin. What does the term 'high-intensity' mean in current dyslipidemia guidance?

options.A: It denotes a regimen expected to lower LDL-C by at least 50%; the actual response can vary and should be assessed with follow-up LDL-C testing and adherence review.
options.B: It denotes a statin that is taken more often than moderate-intensity therapy, with dosing frequency defining the intensity regardless of the expected LDL-C reduction.
options.C: It refers mainly to the medication's acquisition cost and tablet strength rather than the expected percentage reduction in LDL-C achieved during treatment.
options.D: It guarantees that clients receiving the regimen will reach the same absolute LDL-C concentration even when baseline values, adherence, and individual response differ.

rationale: The 2026 ACC/AHA multisociety dyslipidemia guideline categorizes statin intensity by expected percentage LDL-C reduction: high-intensity therapy is expected to lower LDL-C by at least 50%, moderate-intensity therapy by 30% to 49%, and low-intensity therapy by less than 30%. The guideline also states that the magnitude of LDL-C lowering varies in clinical practice and that follow-up LDL-C assessment is used to evaluate treatment response and adherence. Therefore A is correct. B and C misstate how intensity is defined, and D converts an expected relative effect into a guaranteed identical absolute result.
educational_objective: Interpret high-intensity statin therapy as an expected LDL-C reduction of at least 50% and verify the individual therapeutic response with follow-up lipid assessment rather than assuming a uniform result.
source_organization: American College of Cardiology / American Heart Association and partner societies
source_document_title: 2026 ACC/AHA/AACVPR/ABC/ACPM/ADA/AGS/APhA/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia
source_version_date: Originally published March 13, 2026; current guideline accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: §4.2.1.1 Statins, Synopsis and Table 6: high-intensity statin therapy is expected to reduce LDL-C by ≥50%, moderate-intensity by 30%-49%, and low-intensity by <30%; actual LDL-C lowering varies with patient population and adherence, and follow-up LDL-C assessment is used to assess response and adherence.
source_claim_supported: High-intensity statin therapy is defined by an expected LDL-C reduction of at least 50%, while individual response varies and should be confirmed rather than assumed.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: apply knowledge of medication therapeutic effects; evaluate response to therapy; provide medication education.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four options as substantive interpretations of statin intensity with comparable length.
Preserved the ≥50% definition while separating expected class effect from individual follow-up response.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches the 2026 guideline definition. Options are tightly length-matched and no absolute cue or second defensible interpretation remains.
